QuestionStmt.S: Two identical long parallel wires carry currents $I_1$ and $I_2$ such that $I_1 > I_2$. When the currents are in the same direction, the magnetic field at a point midway between the wires is $8 \times 10^{-6}$ T. If the direction of $I_2$ is reversed, the field becomes $3.2 \times 10^{-5}$ T. The ratio of $I_2$ to $I_1$ is

Solution.S:
Magnetic field due to each wire at midpoint: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$.

When currents are in same direction, fields oppose:

$$B_1 - B_2 = 8 \times 10^{-6}$$

$$\frac{\mu_0}{2\pi r}(I_1 - I_2) = 8 \times 10^{-6} \quad \text{(i)}$$

When $I_2$ is reversed, fields add:

$$B_1 + B_2 = 3.2 \times 10^{-5}$$

$$\frac{\mu_0}{2\pi r}(I_1 + I_2) = 3.2 \times 10^{-5} \quad \text{(ii)}$$

Dividing (i) by (ii):

$$\frac{I_1 - I_2}{I_1 + I_2} = \frac{8 \times 10^{-6}}{3.2 \times 10^{-5}} = \frac{8}{32} = \frac{1}{4}$$

$$4I_1 - 4I_2 = I_1 + I_2 \Rightarrow 3I_1 = 5I_2 \Rightarrow \frac{I_2}{I_1} = \frac{3}{5}$$

Thus $I_2 : I_1 = 3 : 5$, which corresponds to option C.
